title: Telemetry aggregator hotpatch for high-cardinality tenant causing dashboard blanks
creator: Ethan Marshall
description: A customer on Dedicated reported repeated dashboard blanking and missing metric series during an end-of-quarter batch job. The root cause appears to be an eviction storm in the telemetry aggregator process that correlates with a single high-cardinality tenant emitting spikes of unique series keys. When the aggregator thrashes, it drops spans and timeseries indexes, which causes live-panel tiles to surface no data and tracing gaps for affected traces. This ticket tracks the hotpatch (in-rack) mitigation, validation, and permanent fixes planned for the runtime and telemetry ingestion layers.
reproduction_steps: Provision a dedicated tenant configuration with high-cardinality synthetic workload (per-request unique tags).
Run a bursty batch workload that opens thousands of unique endpoint labels within 10 minutes.
Observe telemetry-aggregator logs for OOM-like eviction messages and metric index removals.
Open Console live-panels and dashboards for the tenant; observe blank/No Data tiles and missing trace spans in timeframe.
Correlate with sampling and shard allocation logs to confirm aggregation instability.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:12 - initial alert from RedTier SRE after customer escalated via Support (ticket SUP-9943).
Aggregator logs show repeated 'evicting-series' events with >10k series churn/sec during the burst window; memory usage climbs then GC/eviction loop observed.
Heap snapshots indicate internal index map growth followed by aggressive truncation; this leaves index pointers dangling and downstream consumers see tombstoned time series.
Trace pipeline shows sampled spans accepted by ingestion service but lost at aggregator boundary due to index GC race; trace IDs appear in ingress but not in downstream span index store.
Repro locally with load generator using same cardinality pattern; confirmed high churn triggers identical eviction logs and console blanking.
decision_logs: 2026-03-11 11:00 - Triage: apply in-cluster hotpatch to telemetry-aggregator to add a short circuit that preserves recent index buckets under eviction to avoid dangling pointers (agreed by SRE + Runtime leads).
2026-03-11 14:30 - Rollback plan prepared: if hotpatch increases memory beyond safe thresholds, revert to previous aggregator binary and re-route heavy tenants to warm pool (manual).
2026-03-13 16:00 - After canary validation, schedule staggered roll-out to affected Dedicated racks; coordinate with Support for customer notifications.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:05 - James Ortega (SRE): Customer reported sudden blanks at 08:45 UTC; initial mitigation was to increase aggregator retention temporarily. Observed short-term relief but blanks returned when next burst happened.

2026-03-11 11:10 - Priya Desai (assignee): Root cause looks like index GC race under eviction. Working on a conservative hotpatch that quarantines recently-referenced buckets for 30s to avoid pointer invalidation.
2026-03-12 03:00 - Priya Desai: Canary deployment completed to cluster canary-5. No blanking events observed during two peak windows; memory increase ~8% under synthetic load (within threshold).

2026-03-13 09:20 - Lina Voss (Support): Customer was notified of canary and accepted a staged rollout; provided temporary workaround to throttle cardinality by dropping nonessential tags in the agent config.
2026-03-14 08:45 - Ethan Marshall (creator): Peer review requested for PR #1284; request approval from runtime-maintainers and SRE for production rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Hotpatch merged and smoke-tested in production canary clusters with no further dashboard blanking for the reproduced workload.
Affected Dedicated racks receive staged rollout with rollback playbook validated.
Permanent fix design documented: (a) index memory accounting, (b) eviction backpressure to ingestion, (c) shard rebalancing policy improvements.
Automated regression test added to telemetry load harness to exercise high-cardinality churn and assert no grave eviction races.
Customer receives postmortem and validation that their dashboards are stable for 72 hours after rollout.
resolution_summary: Hotpatch (PR #1284) applied to canary on 2026-03-12 and promoted to affected Dedicated racks on 2026-03-13 after validation. Short-term mitigation reduced dashboard blanking incidents to zero for the reproduced workload and for the customer's observed bursts. Next steps: implement index memory accounting and ingestion backpressure (tracked in ENG-721900) and add long-term regression tests. Customer notified and monitoring window opened for 72h. Remaining work planned as follow-ups.
